title: Tell certification which row of the layout to fix

blocks.text: Certifying a new link means trying your layout against every sample message in the host's specification. When a sample doesn't come out right, the person fixing the layout wants one answer: which row to look at first.

Write `LayoutCheck.firstWrongField` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/LayoutCheck.java`. It gets the layout, the sample's bytes, and the value the specification documents for each field of the sample. It returns the number of the field whose row to fix first, or 0 when the layout reads the sample exactly as documented.
The tests use a purchase sample in an ASCII layout and break the layout in different ways. Some of the broken layouts make `unpack` throw, and some don't. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: a layout that reads the sample exactly as documented has nothing to fix
a row one digit too long makes the unpack fail at a later field, and the row to fix is the first field read wrong, not the field the error names
a row one digit too short shifts every later field without any error, so an unpack that succeeds can still be wrong
a documented field the layout never read is wrong too, even when every field read before it matches

origin.section: 13.7 An Unpack Error Points Past the Field That Is Wrong

concepts: An unpack error names a field after the wrong one, and an unpack can succeed with shifted values; the first field whose value is wrong is the row to fix.
The bytes carry no field boundaries, so a receiver whose layout differs in one field reads every later field from the wrong place.
